title: Speaking the family’s language
description: Start from familiar situations and your own gaps, when understanding already works but answering is still hard.

blocks.text: A person grew up around the family’s language, understands familiar speech, but struggles to answer or to choose the verb form. A course for a complete beginner doesn’t allow for that unevenness.

quote.text: I’m a heritage speaker and my biggest challenge other than vocab is understanding how to properly conjugate. I’ve struggled to find an app/resource that solely focuses on this without first trying to explain the basics that I already have a grasp on (like how to say “hello”).

blocks.text: Start from what is already understood

It starts with a short conversation on a familiar topic and a choice of the variety of the language. From that, exercises are picked for specific gaps: forms, vocabulary or understanding faster speech. The basic explanations stay available without having to go through the whole course.

The first version is worth making for one specific language community and testing with people whose family experience differs. The general label “family language” guarantees no common level or set of topics. This scenario could be a route inside an existing course.
